stem: A construction firm placed a governance-mode retention period on a set of contract documents in Amazon S3, and separately placed a legal hold on one document that is now part of active litigation. An administrator with the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission and the correct request header successfully deletes several documents that were only under the governance-mode retention period, but the same delete attempt fails on the document under legal hold. Which TWO statements explain this correctly? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Legal holds automatically expire as soon as the associated governance-mode retention period ends
Compliance-mode retention would have allowed the same bypass permission to succeed
The s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission and header let an authorized principal override a governance-mode retention period
The administrator's root user status, rather than the bypass permission, is what allowed the deletions
A legal hold blocks deletion independently of any governance-mode bypass and must be removed on its own before the object can be deleted

rationale: The s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission, combined with the matching request header, is what lets an authorized principal override a governance-mode retention period, which is why the administrator succeeded on the documents that only had that protection. A legal hold is independent of retention periods and their bypass permission; it must be explicitly removed on its own before the object can be deleted, which is why the same delete attempt failed on the document under legal hold. A legal hold does not expire automatically alongside a retention period; the two are managed and removed separately. Compliance mode never allows a bypass for any principal, including the root user, so it would not have let the same permission succeed. The scenario does not depend on the administrator being the root user; it depends on holding the specific s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission and header, which any authorized principal could hold.
